Subject: Pilot capacity ask — short, phased headroom and autoscale waiver

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the model latency profile on Dedicated looked great. We have a short, time-boxed integration pilot (Phase A) that needs a predictable reserved window plus the ability to burst above the reservation for a limited sweep. High level:

- Window: 2027-06-01 through 2027-06-10 (10 days) with two 6-hour daily surge windows (09:00–15:00 PDT) for load validation.
- Baseline reserved capacity: equivalent of 12 GPUs (A100 class) continuously for the window.
- Burst requirement: up to +40% capacity during the daily 6-hour windows for synthetic load runs (we will coordinate exact times).
- Business reason: rapid throughput validation for latency-sensitive checkout flows (pilot is time-sensitive due to marketing cadence).

We understand Redwood's autoscale safety controls; for the pilot we'd like a temporary waiver so HealthSprint can burst without being pre-empted by standard throttles. We'll accept a firm cost cap and a telemetry gating requirement. Attached: a short headroom spreadsheet and a draft MOU.

Can you confirm feasibility and what guardrails you’d want to approve a waiver? If this looks feasible we'll route to procurement for an addendum (deal HS-4621).

Thanks — Samantha

Thanks for the heads-up. I reviewed the spreadsheet — looks reasonable but a few infra constraints to flag before approving any autoscale waiver:

- We cannot allow unbounded burst for multi-tenant pools; a waiver must be bounded by an absolute instance limit and a token/cost ceiling.
- Proposed safe guardrails:
  * Max burst nodes: +40% capped at +5 additional nodes (whichever is lower).
  * Burst window enforcement: daily windows enforced by a scheduler; if HealthSprint misses the start time, burst won't be auto-triggered.
  * Burst_budget: monetary cap per day and for the entire window (suggest $6k/day, $60k total as an initial number to align with spreadsheet).
  * Telemetry hooks: must send a token-level rate metric to our tracing endpoint every 60s during surges.
  * Preflight test: 1-hour smoke run on 2027-05-29 to validate KV cache priming and cold start characteristics.

Operational notes: we'll need a runbook and a rollback trigger. I attached a short ops runbook outline. If product signs off, we can implement a temporally-scoped autoscale policy that only applies to HealthSprint's pool id (non-global change).

Cheers,
Marcus Lin

Appreciate the detail. From a product/prioritization perspective, HealthSprint's use case aligns with our low-latency showcase goals and the pilot could convert quickly if performance checks pass. I'm willing to approve a time-boxed carve (subject to the infra guardrails Marcus outlined) if the following are in place:

- A telemetry SLA: real-time token rate + 95th latency pushed to our console with 1-minute granularity during surges.
- Cost cap enforcement: procurement to accept the daily and total cap; infra to enforce at the policy level (hard stop).
- Escalation path: named on-call from HealthSprint during surge windows and a Redwood on-call contact.
- Security quick check: HealthSprint to complete a focused security Q that we'll limit in scope (not full SOC2) — they attached it in the first thread but please send the completed PDF before preflight.

If all that lands, product can mark this pilot as approved and we'll prioritize the small allocation (I can sign the internal approval).

Thanks — Laura
